stair_landing_derivation: A stair's landing is as deep as the flight Deli Counter draws is wide: agent_contract.stair_flight_width(), min_corridor_width_m plus one nav_bake.cell_size_m, 1.2 m at this contract -- presets.STAIR_FLIGHT_WIDTH and stairwell.LANDING_DEPTH both read it (0.215.0; LANDING_DEPTH was a literal 1.2 recorded as a game-readability default, the same number). The rule is the building code's: IBC 2018 section 1011.6 gives a landing a depth, measured in the direction of travel, of the stairway's width or 48 in (1.219 m), whichever is less. The 48 in cap is left out on purpose: it assumes a human body, and this contract sets the body, so a wider character gets a wider flight and a deeper landing together. A library stair drawn at another width keeps the generator's landing; the code's rule per stair (its own width) would move every narrower library stair's reservation, and is not taken.
vault_aperture_derivation: The round vault door's opening is min_door_width_m rounded up to the next 0.1 m by min_headroom_m plus 0.1, on the floor: 1.3 x 2.1 m, sill 0, at this contract (agent_contract.vault_aperture(); vault_room.APERTURE and spec_types' vault default read it since 0.215.0 -- both were literals with a comment giving this rule). The sill is 0 because 0.15 put a step above unassisted_step_max_m in the doorway. Deli Counter writes the opening into the vault door's slot (fit.openings) and Zoo builds the door to it; Zoo's vault_forms.DEFAULT_OPENING serves only a standalone build that describes no opening.
